paths.path: ~/.config/flycast/emu.cfg ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/flycast/emu.cfg when that variable is set; ./emu.cfg only if neither XDG_CONFIG_HOME nor HOME is usable). emu.cfg is read from the user dir first, then system dirs $XDG_CONFIG_DIRS/flycast, /etc/flycast and /etc/xdg/flycast, but only the user dir is ever written
paths.naming: INI. Controller mapping lives in two places: (1) [input] section maple device/port assignments - GamepadDevice::SaveMaplePorts writes [input] maple_<unique_id> = <maple port 0-3>; SDL gamepads get unique ids sdl_joystick_<SDL instance number>, so the keys are maple_sdl_joystick_0..3, exactly the `[input] maple_sdl_joystick_ID` contract Lunchbox writes for private configs (players 1-4 -> native ports 0-3, unselected joysticks -1); (2) button/axis bindings in mapping files mappings/<api>_<device name>[-<unique_id>][_<gameId>][_arcade].cfg under the config dir, or the first directory of [config] Dreamcast.MappingsPath (semicolon/quoted dir list); mapping files are INIs with [emulator] mapping_name/dead_zone/saturation/rumble_power/version and [combo] bindN = codes:option:sequential plus a trigger list (file version 4 on master; Lunchbox's pinned writer emits version 3). Per-game options are stored as a section named by the game ID inside the same emu.cfg, not a separate file

paths.path: ~/.local/share/flycast/ ($XDG_DATA_HOME/flycast when set) - the data dir root, no extra data/ subfolder. Per-game VMUs and shared VMUs sit side by side; Dreamcast console flash dc_nvmem.bin and NAOMI/Atomiswave nvmem/eeprom/card files land here too. User overrides: [config] Dreamcast.VMUPath for VMUs, [config] Dreamcast.SavePath for arcade saves
paths.naming: Shared VMUs: vmu_save_<port>.bin (port letter+slot, e.g. vmu_save_A1.bin, vmu_save_C1.bin). Per-game VMU is ON by default ([config] Dreamcast.PerGameVmu = true): <gameId>_vmu_save_A1.bin where gameId is the disc product number with the characters space / \ : * ? | < > " replaced by '_' (e.g. MK-51164_vmu_save_A1.bin); content without a game ID falls back to the legacy <content fileName>_vmu_save_A1.bin prefix. Resolution order: Dreamcast.VMUPath, then writable data dir, then read-only data dir, then legacy config dir (old .reicast layout). NAOMI/Atomiswave: <content fileName>.nvmem flash, <content fileName>.nvmem2 second Atomiswave flash, JVS <content fileName>.eeprom (+-main.eeprom for Derby multiboard main board), <content fileName>-p<N>.card / .card memory cards - all derived from the content file name in the data dir
evidence: source:core/oslib/oslib.cpp hostfs::getVmuPath (vmu_save_<port>.bin, <gameId>_vmu_save_A1.bin with INVALID_CHARS " /\:*?|<>\"", PerGameVmu, VMUPath override, legacy get_game_save_prefix and .reicast config-dir fallbacks)

paths.path: ~/.local/share/flycast/ (data dir root, next to the VMU files); override directory list [config] Dreamcast.SavestatePath
paths.naming: <content fileName without extension>[_<slot>].state - the slot suffix _1.._99 is omitted for slot 0; rollback/netplay states append .state.net, quicksave temp buffers .state.tmp. The PNG screenshot is embedded in the rzip-compressed file behind a SavestateHeader, not written alongside. Slots cycle through [config] Dreamcast.SavestateSlot and [config] Dreamcast.AutoSaveState triggers a final state on exit

paths.path: ~/.local/share/flycast/ (data dir root): dc_boot.bin for the Dreamcast; arcade BIOS zips naomi.zip, naomigd.zip, naomi2.zip(?), awbios.zip, hod2bios.zip, f355bios.zip for NAOMI/Atomiswave. Search order: [config] Dreamcast.BiosPath directories, then the data dir, then [config] Dreamcast.ContentPath directories
paths.naming: Dreamcast boot ROM must be named dc_boot.bin (findFlash prefix dc_ over patterns %boot.bin;%bios.bin, i.e. dc_boot.bin then a plain bios.bin); if absent Flycast uses its HLE BIOS. The console flash/VMU area file dc_nvmem.bin is generated on first run (load %nvmem.bin, save nvmem.bin with the dc_ prefix). Arcade BIOS archive names come from the BIOS[] table (naomi, naomigd, naomi2, awbios, hod2bios) resolved as <name>.zip or <name>.7z; the wiki lists naomi.zip (almost all NAOMI games), hod2bios.zip, awbios.zip, f355bios.zip and says NAOMI/Atomiswave BIOS files are required while the Dreamcast BIOS is optional. Lunchbox DB firmware_rules already carries flycast roots for this (crates/lunchbox-app/src/firmware.rs: linux ~/.local/share/flycast, flatpak ~/.var/app/org.flycast.Flycast/data/flycast)
evidence: source:core/hw/flashrom/nvmem.cpp getRomPrefix (dc_/naomi_/naomi2_/awbios_ prefixes), loadFiles (sys_rom->Load(getRomPrefix(), "%boot.bin;%bios.bin", "bootrom") with loadHle fallback), loadFlash (%nvmem.bin), saveFiles (dc_nvmem.bin)
source:core/oslib/oslib.cpp findFlash (Dreamcast.BiosPath dirs, get_readonly_data_path, Dreamcast.ContentPath dirs) and findNaomiBios
docs:https://github.com/TheArcadeStriker/flycast-wiki/wiki/Getting-started-with-Flycast (dc_boot.bin naming and BIOS zip table, Dreamcast BIOS optional / NAOMI+Atomiswave required)

linux.notes: Lunchbox launches Flycast with a private XDG_CONFIG_HOME pointing at a session-owned flycast/emu.cfg (docs/FLYCAST_STANDALONE_PROGRESS.md 'Native Linux config selection' + 'Private config preparation'); user config is never overwritten and private writes stay session-local. Native VMU/nvmem/savestate files keep their data-dir locations.
